intro: The AI boom's growing pains are getting harder to ignore: Google is watching its search cash cow stumble as AI Mode queries surge but don't pay the bills, Canva just cut 22% of its workforce in a gut-punch restructuring, and data centers are now literally bolting retired jet engines from Boeing 747s onto their facilities because the power grid can't keep up. Meanwhile, the governance alarms are ringing louder — from Australia warning it's "sleepwalking into another robodebt" with unchecked government AI, to Anthropic building cryptographic proof systems so you can verify which model actually produced an output — today's digest is a snapshot of an industry sprinting forward while scrambling to build the guardrails behind it.

stories.title: Argentinian artist seals living ecosystems in closed containers as climate art
stories.summary: A short film profiles Argentinian artist-engineer Joaquín Fargas and his 'Biosphere Project,' which seals natural ecosystems inside completely closed containers where only heat and light can enter or exit, serving as living metaphors for Earth's fragility.
stories.opinion: A poetic, visually striking intersection of art and ecology — worth including if the newsletter has room for a creative/culture angle, though it has no AI or tech-industry connection.

stories.title: New UEFI bootkit 'BlackX' infects fully patched Windows machines via lingering Secure Boot flaw
stories.summary: A UEFI bootkit called BlackX has compromised fully patched Windows systems by exploiting the same Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE-2022-21894) that BlackLotus used in 2023. Despite multiple rounds of patches, Microsoft's mitigation process never fully revoked trust in older vulnerable boot managers, leaving a gap that attackers exploited.
stories.opinion: A significant security story that raises uncomfortable questions about whether Microsoft's multi-year Secure Boot mitigation strategy is fundamentally broken. Relevant to any audience tracking endpoint security.

stories.title: Australian thinktank warns government is 'sleepwalking into another robodebt' with AI use
stories.summary: Australia's Centre for Public Integrity warned the Albanese government that insufficient transparency and oversight of algorithms and AI in federal decision-making risks repeating a robodebt-like scandal, calling for a mandatory audit and public register of all automated decision-making systems.
stories.opinion: A politically charged warning with direct parallels to a real past scandal — strong governance angle for readers interested in public-sector AI accountability.

stories.title: MIT Tech Review argues 'data lineage' is the new security perimeter for agentic AI
stories.summary: A sponsored MIT Technology Review article (with Cyberhaven) argues that traditional security approaches fail for agentic AI workflows where multiple agents pass data without human oversight, and that tracking data lineage — how data moves, is copied, and transformed across agents — is essential for governance and trust.
stories.opinion: Conceptually interesting framing of agentic AI security, but readers should note this is a vendor-sponsored piece promoting Cyberhaven's product category.

stories.title: Anthropic building open-source system to cryptographically prove which AI model produced an output
stories.summary: Anthropic is developing FlashProve, an open-source system that uses published model 'fingerprints' to cryptographically verify which AI model generated a given output, without revealing proprietary weights. The system aims to prevent secret model swapping and let third parties audit model claims. Code and specs are on GitHub but deployment is not yet planned.
stories.opinion: A trust-infrastructure play that could become important as AI model provenance grows in regulatory and commercial significance. The open-source approach is notable.

stories.title: Apple opens Siri AI to third-party developers in new beta preview
stories.summary: Apple released a developer preview of Siri AI in its latest betas, letting app developers build custom actions and multi-step 'skills' into the rebuilt assistant. App Store submissions won't begin until spring. The article also notes Google is bundling AI features inseparably with Google Search for K-12 school accounts, and CrowdStrike is developing a kill switch for rogue AI agents.
stories.opinion: The Siri AI developer opening is the headline item — it signals Apple's strategy for making its assistant an extensible platform. The Google K-12 bundling is a notable policy story in its own right.

stories.title: Sam Altman rebrands as 'Ram Altman' after backlash over PC memory comments
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman responded to criticism of his remarks calling personal DRAM 'quite terrible' by rebranding himself 'Ram Altman' on X during election night, insisting his comments were taken out of context. The backdrop is a global DRAM shortage driven by AI data center demand, with Intel expecting shortages through next year and SK Hynix predicting they could last until 2030.
stories.opinion: A lighter story on its surface, but the underlying DRAM shortage is a real and growing constraint on consumer hardware pricing — the Altman drama is the hook for a substantive supply-chain issue.

stories.title: Australian social cohesion report finds cost of living and AI now top future concerns
stories.summary: The 2026 Scanlon Foundation social cohesion report finds growing pessimism, financial stress, and distrust of government among Australians, with cost of living and AI overtaking climate change and war as top concerns about the future, even as support for immigration and multiculturalism remains high.
stories.opinion: Notable as a signal that AI anxiety has crossed from a tech-sector concern into mainstream public worry in Australia, displacing previously dominant issues.

stories.title: Data centers turn to retired jet engines as grid connection waits stretch to seven years
stories.summary: Facing years-long waits for grid connections, data center operators including xAI, OpenAI, and Crusoe are converting retired jet engines to burn natural gas for on-site power. Supplier ProEnergy rebuilds GE engines from Boeing jets. A jet-powered facility can run in 24 months versus ~7 years for a 100 MW grid connection in Northern Virginia, but the engines are less efficient, more polluting, and likely a stopgap.
stories.opinion: A vivid illustration of how urgent AI power demand is reshaping energy infrastructure — the image of Boeing jet engines powering data centers captures the improvisation happening at the frontier.

stories.title: Google's AI Mode queries are growing fast but monetizing poorly, weighing on search revenue
stories.summary: Alphabet reported search queries growing at their fastest rate in five years, but search revenue growth slowed to 12% YoY in Q3 (from ~17% prior quarter) and paid click growth fell from 13% to 8%. AI Mode queries are growing strongly but monetize at lower rates than traditional searches. Shares fell ~14% post-earnings. The company plans ~$200B in AI infrastructure spending this year.
stories.opinion: This may be the first concrete evidence that AI is disrupting Google's core search economics from within — a significant inflection point for the company and the broader AI business model debate.

stories.title: Canva cuts 1,200+ jobs — 22% of workforce — in major restructure
stories.summary: Australian design platform Canva is cutting or relocating more than 1,200 jobs (22% of its global workforce). CEO Melanie Perkins called it 'without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history.' The cuts reflect a broader pattern of significant workforce reductions across software companies.
stories.opinion: A major layoff at one of the biggest private tech companies — notable both for its scale and as a data point in the ongoing tech workforce contraction trend.

stories.title: Cybersecurity VC Ballistic Ventures seeks $490M amid AI-driven security boom
stories.summary: Ballistic Ventures, co-founded by former Kleiner Perkins partner Ted Schlein, is raising $490M across two funds ($360M flagship, $130M Fund B). U.S. cybersecurity startups raised $11.5B in 2025 and AI-enabled companies accounted for 72% of U.S. cybersecurity venture deals through May 2026. Notable portfolio exits include Talon (to Palo Alto Networks) and Pangea (to CrowdStrike).
stories.opinion: Useful as a market-signal story — the fundraise size and the 72% AI-enabled deal stat together paint a picture of how central AI has become to cybersecurity investing.

stories.title: Nexus Mods introduces mandatory AI disclosure for all new mod uploads
stories.summary: Nexus Mods, the largest PC gaming mod repository, is requiring all new uploads to declare whether AI was used, with AI-tagged mods needing a public explanation of how and where AI was utilized. Owner Victor Folmann positioned the site as 'pro-human creativity' but stopped short of banning AI mods, arguing that AI is already embedded throughout the creative process and a ban would just push usage underground. The site confirmed it will not use uploaded mods to train AI models.
stories.opinion: A pragmatic middle path in the AI-in-creative-work debate — transparency over prohibition. The reasoning that bans drive underground use mirrors arguments in other creative communities.

> 12 cluttered boxes, and no idea where to start.
> no clue what you yourself are looking at, and why.

I like how Shopify's CEO calls it "slop grenades."

I spent an entire day figuring out how to un-slop those reports, whether you are the one sending or receiving them.

Here's how:

Step 1. Copy the prompt from my guide: https://t.co/4GBb1RcBDp

It has my free GitHub repo link. No, it's not technical

→ If you're making a new report
Copy the "make a page" prompt from the guide.

→ If you are fixing an existing one
Copy the "fix a page" prompt from the same guide.

Step 2. Attach your AI slop report to Claude.

> Your meeting notes.
> Your spreadsheet.
> Your existing report.
> Or an overwhelmingly slopped page someone just sent you to do the job, they are supposed to.

Step 3. Tell Claude (specifically) WHO will read it.

Your prompt "For Dana, my colleague" is a NO-go
Be painfully specific like: "For Dana, my CFO".
Then tell it what Dana needs to do after reading.

Step 4. The report needs to only have ONE job.

→ Either to make a decision? Put the ask on top.
→ Or to catch up? Lead with 3 or 4 numbers.
→ Or to learn a process? One step per screen.
→ Or to approve a proposal? One idea per slide.

Step 5. Now, go back to Step 1 and paste the prompt from the guide.

Do not ignore that prompt, it is going to un-slop by Claude reading my rules, then building the page for your reader.

Don't worry. You install nothing.

The prompts, before-and-after examples, and 7 types of pages are here:

https://t.co/4GBb1RcBDp

Take the last report you sent. Fix that one first.

tweet_headlines.author: GrokBotRadar
tweet_headlines.headline: One Grok Bot audit uncovered __78% of 965M monthly tokens__ spent on bots re-reading themselves — here's how to check yours.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
How to tell if Grok Bot changed your usage, or your BOTS did 👀

Mine was back at 45% this morning with a day left. My Oct 25 export: 965 MILLION tokens, 78% of them my Bots re-reading 😳

The play: Tokens per day vs your weekly % > Export > ask your Bot

Here's how 👇

✅ Go to https://t.co/EgtMSQWvLo and open Usage
✅ Look at Tokens per day for this week
✅ Tokens flat but your % jumped? That points to the meter
✅ Tokens jumped too? Your Bots did more
✅ Scroll to Usage events and hit Export (top right)
✅ Upload the file to your main Bot and paste:

"Check this usage file. Compare my tokens per day across the week, tell me which days jumped, and what I should slow down. Don't change anything yet."

The catch ⚠️
→ The export isn't an official feature. It could move or disappear
→ No per-Bot column. It shows re-reading, not WHICH Bot
→ Your email is in every row. Don't post the file
→ Your Bot reading the file costs usage too
→ Some people's % looked glitchy this weekend. Trust today's number, not Sunday's

Don't 🚫
→ Cancel or upgrade over one bad day
→ Screenshot the export with your email showing

Check the chart before you decide anything.

Reply: did your tokens jump, or just your %? 👇

Bookmark this 🔖 The full fix list is in the article 👇

tweet_headlines.source_text:
Update: My Grokbot usage reset this morning at 7 AM.

I spent about 15 minutes talking with my bot about how quickly I hit my limit last week, cleaning up our processes to reduce token usage, and removing a few unnecessary bots.

That conversation alone used 9% of my entire weekly allowance. The irony is that I burned nearly 10% of my weekly usage just discussing how to use less of it moving forward.

I genuinely love Grokbot. It’s easily my favorite agentic AI tool I’ve used, but this level of usage just isn’t sustainable. If a simple conversation about improving efficiency eats up that much of my allowance, I can’t realistically rely on it for the rest of the week.

Starting to seriously consider alternatives like Muse or Dots unfortunately.

tweet_headlines.author: nifinet
tweet_headlines.headline: How Grok bots scrape __leads from competitor giveaways__ on X and LinkedIn, for free
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Every lead magnet your competitors post on X and LinkedIn is a few hundred leads you can scrape with Grok @bot, for free.

Today I'm giving away the 3 bots that do it, plus the prompt that sets them up.

We ran them on one cold email giveaway with 298 replies: they read 172 people and came back with 6 worth an email, first emails written.

Finder picks the giveaways and the competitor or creator posts on X in your niche with 50+ replies. Here's our first run, on a cold email giveaway with 298 replies:

- Finder saved 172 people, with bio and website, before hitting the read limit we'd set for the run
- Sorter tagged 29 possible buyers, 14 vendors, 8 creators and 1 bot, and kept 1 person per company
- 120 bios were too thin to judge, so Sorter left them off the shortlist
- 6 made the shortlist, 2 high fit and 4 medium
- Drafter read up to 3 public pages on each and wrote an email and a LinkedIn note for all 6, each opening on 1 public fact about the person

We've connected https://t.co/shO8OijHTg to the bots, so the same loop runs on LinkedIn: point them at any post, they pull everyone who commented or reacted, and Drafter writes to the ones who fit.

Approve a draft and https://t.co/shO8OijHTg finds the email and sends it for you through Overloop AI.

Comment "BOT" and I'll send you the repo (yeah, I'm aware of the irony lol).

tweet_headlines.author: 0xMfox
tweet_headlines.headline: Anthropic renamed Max 20x to Ultra and dropped the 5-hour limit — but only for __verified accounts__
tweet_headlines.source_text:
You can pay Claude $200 a month and still not be trusted. One bar on your Usage page tells you.

Anthropic renamed Max 20x to Ultra and dropped its 5-hour limit, but only for verified accounts. The $100 plan is now just Max and keeps the 5-hour limit.

Weekly limits didn't move on either. So on Ultra the weekly cap is the only wall left.

My worst day in Claude Code cost $208, and my average week costs $182. Now nothing stops a day like that halfway.

How I run Ultra now:

1. Open Settings > Usage. If there's no "Current session" bar, you're verified and the 5-hour limit is gone
2. If the bar is still there, you're on a temporary limit. Anthropic verifies you on its own from your account and payment history, and a phone check doesn't count
3. Watch the weekly bar. Fable has a separate one
4. Give each day about 14% of the week, then switch to Sonnet until tomorrow
5. Move file reading to Haiku with one file, it's in the reply

On the $100 Max nothing changed. OpenAI doubled the limits on its $100 Pro tier the same week.

tweet_headlines.author: AISystems_hq
tweet_headlines.headline: 10 GitHub repos for __AI-powered video transcription, editing, and dubbing__ most creators have never heard of
tweet_headlines.source_text:
GitHub is an absolute GOLDMINE for YouTubers and podcasters.

I found 10 insane repos that can help you transcribe, edit, dub and voice your videos using AI.

Most creators have no idea these exist.

Bookmark this:

1. Buzz
Transcribes and translates audio and video offline, on your own computer, powered by Whisper. Exports TXT, SRT and VTT.
chidiwilliams/buzz

2. WhisperX
Whisper with word-level timestamps and speaker labels, so you know who said what and when.
m-bain/whisperX

3. auto-editor
Cuts the silence and dead space out of raw footage automatically, by reading the audio's loudness.
WyattBlue/auto-editor

4. pyvideotrans
Translates a video into another language: transcribes it, translates the subtitles and dubs it with AI voices.
jianchang512/pyvideotrans

5. Chatterbox
Open-source text-to-speech from Resemble AI with voice cloning, in 23+ languages.
resemble-ai/chatterbox

6. Remotion
Make videos with code in React, or turn an idea into a video using your agent. Good for intros, captions and templates.
remotion-dev/remotion

7. Fabric
A library of crowdsourced AI prompts it calls patterns, with one use case being pulling the best parts out of a podcast or YouTube video.
danielmiessler/Fabric

8. rembg
Removes the background from any image, handy for thumbnails.
danielgatis/rembg

9. Upscayl
Free, open-source AI image upscaler for Mac, Windows and Linux, for sharper thumbnails and stills.
upscayl/upscayl

10. ComfyUI
A node-based app for image, video and audio generation with open models, running on your own machine.
Comfy-Org/ComfyUI

Some of these want a decent GPU, and check each model's license before you use it commercially.

Which one are you adding to your workflow first?
